subject: psychiatry
title: Reversible Dementias, Neurodegenerative Conditions, and Cholinesterase Inhibitors

steps.tx: **Pseudodementia**, or depressive cognitive impairment, represents reversible cognitive deficits secondary to severe major depression in elderly patients. Clinically distinguished from true dementia, patients frequently answer bedside questions with abrupt 'I do not know' statements, show acute onset, and demonstrate full cognitive recovery following antidepressant therapy.
steps.say: Pseudodementia is cognitive impairment caused by severe depression. Patients answer 'I do not know' and recover fully with antidepressant treatment.

left.title: Depressive Pseudodementia
points: Abrupt, rapid onset of cognitive complaints
Answers 'I do not know' without trying
Exaggerates and emphasizes memory deficits
Delayed recall improves with structured cueing

right.title: True Alzheimer Dementia
points: Insidious onset with progressive worsening
Attempts questions, producing near-miss errors
Conceals and minimizes cognitive failures
Delayed recall shows zero improvement with cueing

steps.tx: **Normal pressure hydrocephalus**, abbreviated NPH, is a potentially reversible dementia syndrome caused by impaired cerebrospinal fluid absorption at the arachnoid granulations. It is characterized by Hakim's classic clinical triad: gait apraxia ('magnetic gait'), urinary urge incontinence, and insidious cognitive dementia.
steps.say: Normal pressure hydrocephalus features the classic triad of magnetic gait apraxia, urinary incontinence, and dementia, reversible with shunting.

vis.title: Hakim Triad Clinical Progression
rows: Broad-based, shuffling, feet glued to floor
First symptom to appear; highest recovery rate after shunt
Urge incontinence progressing to lack of concern
Second symptom to emerge; moderate recovery rate
Last symptom to emerge; lowest recovery rate after shunt

steps.tx: Picture the older adult who walks as if the floor were magnetised, feet barely leaving the ground in short shuffling steps. The same patient rushes to the toilet with new urgency, then starts forgetting conversations and misplacing everyday items. Gait trouble arriving first, followed by bladder urgency and slowed thinking, forms the **Hakim triad** of normal pressure hydrocephalus. Spotting all three together prompts imaging and a trial of cerebrospinal fluid removal.
steps.say: The Hakim triad combines magnetic shuffling gait, urinary urgency and dementia, with gait usually appearing first.

vis.alt: Older adult shown with a shuffling magnetic gait, urinary urgency and forgetfulness representing the three features of normal pressure hydrocephalus
vis.caption: Magnetic shuffling gait, urinary urgency and cognitive slowing shown together as the three features of normal pressure hydrocephalus. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Diagnostic tap test in NPH** involves the removal of 30 to 50 milliliters of cerebrospinal fluid via lumbar puncture, demonstrating normal opening pressure. A dramatic objective improvement in walking velocity, stride length, and balance within hours following the tap test confirms the diagnosis and predicts successful ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement.
steps.say: A diagnostic lumbar tap removing forty milliliters of CSF with normal opening pressure restores gait speed, predicting ventriculoperitoneal shunt success.

nodes.label: Brain MRI: ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal enlargement
Conduct baseline quantitative timed 10-meter walking test
Perform large-volume lumbar puncture (30 to 50 mL CSF removed)
Repeat walking test: >20% speed improvement justifies surgical VP shunt

steps.tx: **Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease** is a rapidly fatal transmissible spongiform encephalopathy caused by prions, characterized by conversion of normal cellular prion protein PrPC into abnormal beta-sheet rich PrPSc. Patients present with rapidly progressive dementia, multifocal myoclonus triggered by loud sounds, ataxia, and terminal akinetic mutism.
steps.say: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease causes rapid dementia and startle myoclonus driven by infectious prions, leading to death within twelve months.

left.title: Clinical Features
points: Rapidly progressive dementia over weeks to months
Prominent startle-induced myoclonic jerks
Cerebellar ataxia and visual cortical blindness
Death typically within one year of onset

right.title: Diagnostic Tests
points: EEG: periodic synchronous triphasic sharp waves
CSF: elevated 14-3-3 protein & positive RT-QuIC
MRI: cortical ribboning & basal ganglia hyperintensity
Brain biopsy: diffuse spongiform vacuolation

steps.tx: **Diagnostic findings in Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease** on electroencephalography reveal characteristic periodic synchronous biphasic or triphasic sharp wave complexes occurring at 1 to 2 Hertz against a slow background. Brain MRI shows cortical ribboning on diffusion-weighted imaging, while cerebrospinal fluid analysis confirms positive 14-3-3 protein.
steps.say: Diagnostic workup in CJD reveals periodic sharp wave complexes on EEG, cortical ribboning on brain MRI, and positive 14-3-3 protein in CSF.

vis.title: Diagnostic Hallmarks of CJD
rows: Periodic synchronous triphasic sharp waves (1 Hz)
Cortical ribboning & hockey-stick sign in pulvinar
Direct real-time prion protein seed amplification
Non-specific marker of rapid neuronal destruction

steps.tx: **Cholinesterase inhibitors in Alzheimer disease** include donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine, indicated for mild to moderate dementia to compensate for basal forebrain cholinergic deficit. Donepezil is a once-daily selective acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; rivastigmine provides dual inhibition of acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, formulated as a transdermal patch.
steps.say: Cholinesterase inhibitors like donepezil and rivastigmine enhance cholinergic transmission in Alzheimer disease, improving cognition and daily function.

vis.title: Cholinesterase Inhibitor Formulations
rows: Minimal GI side effects via patch route

steps.tx: Scan the repeating waveforms marching across this EEG trace at regular intervals. These **periodic sharp-wave complexes**, often triphasic and synchronous across both hemispheres, are a classic supportive finding in Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease once myoclonus and rapidly progressive dementia have appeared. They do not occur in every patient, so their absence cannot exclude prion disease when the clinical course otherwise fits the diagnosis well.
steps.say: Periodic triphasic sharp waves support Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in a rapidly dementing patient with myoclonus. Their absence, however, does not rule the disease out.

vis.alt: EEG recording in Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease showing periodic synchronous triphasic sharp-wave complexes over a slowed background
vis.caption: EEG recording demonstrating periodic synchronous triphasic sharp-wave complexes in Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Memantine** is an uncompetitive, low-affinity N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist indicated for moderate to severe Alzheimer disease, either as monotherapy or combined with donepezil. By blocking pathologically sustained, low-level glutamate excitotoxicity without interfering with normal physiological neurotransmission, memantine preserves surviving cortical neurons.
steps.say: Memantine blocks pathological NMDA glutamate excitotoxicity, protecting surviving neurons in moderate to severe Alzheimer disease.

left.title: Memantine Mechanism
points: Uncompetitive low-affinity NMDA receptor block
Suppresses chronic glutamate excitotoxicity
Preserves normal physiological synaptic pulses
Approved for moderate to severe dementia

right.title: Combination Synergy
points: Combined with donepezil in advanced stages
Enhances cholinergic tone while dampening glutamate
Slows institutionalization and functional decline
Well tolerated with low incidence of dizziness

steps.tx: **Mini-Mental State Examination**, abbreviated MMSE, is a standardized 30-point bedside screening instrument assessing orientation, immediate registration, attention and calculation, delayed recall, language, and visuospatial construction. A score below 24 indicates clinically significant cognitive impairment, while scores below 10 reflect severe cognitive dementia.
steps.say: The MMSE scores cognitive function from zero to thirty. Scores below twenty-four confirm cognitive impairment, while scores below ten indicate severe dementia.

vis.title: MMSE Cognitive Domains & Scoring
rows: Year, season, date, day, month; country, state, city, hospital, floor
Name three common objects; patient repeats immediately
Serial sevens subtraction or spell 'WORLD' backwards
Recall the three registered objects after 5 minutes
Naming, repetition, 3-stage command, reading, writing, copy pentagons
